blocks.text: A fetch handler can try the network first and use a saved page when that request fails. Limit the rule to the kind of request you intend to handle.

These examples belong in separate files on your own HTTPS or localhost site. Service workers need that trusted origin and cannot run in this site's sandbox. Use browser developer tools to inspect them.

blocks.title: Give navigation an offline fallback

blocks.text: Read the code step by step

items: `addEventListener` waits for the named event before calling the function you pass to it.
`respondWith` supplies the response for an intercepted request. The promise must resolve to a usable Response.

blocks.text: Page navigation uses the network when available. If it fails, a cached offline page or a plain message is returned.

blocks.title: A mistake to avoid
blocks.text: A fallback page does not make every page or every data request available offline.

blocks.title: Your small task
blocks.text: Use the browser offline setting and reload a controlled page.
